newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen hints at arbitration in dispute with Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Yemen hints at arbitration in dispute with Saudi.

text.p: A senior Yemeni minister hinted on Friday his country and Saudi Arabia should turn to international arbitration if negotiations fail to settle a 60-year-old border dispute.
"Both sides have to make concessions," Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdul-Karim al-Iryani told Reuters.
"Suppose one side refuses to concede, what does the other side do. He has to resort to normal legal means because what is the alternative -- we say we will go and use force?, impossible".
Earlier on Friday, Iryani told a news conference the border issue was highly complicated.
"There is no doubt that the border disputes are heated disputes and there is no doubt this is still an obstacle in the the way of completely harmonious relations between the two countries," he said.

Yemen and Saudi Arabia had several minor clashes in the potentially oil and gas-rich border area before they signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the row and set up a committee to demarcate the land and sea borders.

Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh last summer complained the committee was making slow progress and called for a summit with Saudi Arabia to speed up the talks. The committee has met scores of times since 1995.

Yemen's relations with Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, have improved in the last few years. Sanaa angered most Gulf governments when it appeared to side with Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
